title: Coffee, Cappuccino, Decaffeinated, with Non-Dairy Milk

content.title: About
content.content: Decaffeinated cappuccino with non‑dairy milk is a beverage made from roasted coffee beans that have had the caffeine removed, combined with frothed plant‑based milk (soy, oat, almond, etc.). It retains the characteristic aroma and creamy texture while lacking the stimulating effect of caffeine.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Decaffeination is usually performed by water‑process or CO₂ extraction, preserving most flavor compounds.
The name “cappuccino” comes from the color of the Capuchin monks’ robes.
Plant milks add unique notes: oat milk gives a subtle sweetness, soy adds a light nuttiness.
Decaf cappuccino is often chosen by caffeine‑sensitive individuals, pregnant women, and athletes.
In some countries decaffeinated coffee is classified as a separate grade with its own taste ratings.

items.title: Low caffeine content
items.content: Absence of caffeine reduces the risk of anxiety, high blood pressure, and sleep disturbances.

items.title: Antioxidants preserved
items.content: Decaffeination retains polyphenols that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Lactose‑free
items.content: Plant milk contains no lactose, making the drink suitable for lactose‑intolerant individuals.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals
items.content: Soy and oat milks are often fortified with calcium, vitamin D and B‑12, supporting bone and nervous system health.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: Decaf cappuccino contributes to fluid balance without the diuretic effect of caffeine.

items.title: Allergy to plant milk
items.content: Some people may be allergic to soy, almond, or oat milk.

items.title: Added sugars
items.content: Certain ready‑to‑drink mixes can contain added sugars, increasing calorie content.

items.title: Potential contaminants
items.content: Chemical decaffeination methods may leave trace solvent residues if not properly controlled.

items.title: Caloric content
items.content: Plant‑based milks can be more caloric than black coffee.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the decaf cappuccino hot, garnish with cinnamon or cocoa powder. Optional sugar‑free flavored syrups can be added. The drink pairs well with whole‑grain pastries, fruit desserts, and light snacks.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the prepared beverage refrigerated and consume within 24 hours. Store plant milk in its original sealed container at 0‑4 °C. Discard if it develops a sour smell or changes color.
